title: Data centers are allowed at Greenfield business park
brief: Greenfield is the only area Botetourt County has zoned for data centers. Developers still need separate permits to grade land and build. Troutville sets its own zoning rules.

title: What permits does a new building need?
brief: A developer needs building and zoning permits for construction, then an occupancy permit before the building can be used.

title: Operating data centers need fire inspections
brief: The county requires fire prevention permits and an annual inspection by the fire marshal.

title: When does grading need a permit?
brief: A permit is required if work disturbs 5,000 square feet or more. Smaller projects in sensitive areas may also need one.

title: Towns set their own zoning rules
brief: The county ordinance does not apply inside Loudoun’s seven incorporated towns. Check the town boundary, not just the mailing address.

title: Which zoning rules apply to this property?
brief: Check the parcel map and its approval history. Properties along Route 28 can be subject to different versions of the county ordinance.

title: Some Route 28 properties still follow the 1972 rules
brief: Check whether the owner gave up those protections through rezoning or conversion.

title: Three industrial districts require a special zoning approval
brief: A developer generally needs a special exception for a data center in the three districts listed below. Earlier approvals may still apply.

Construction runoff can need state authorization
brief: Count the whole development when checking the one-acre threshold. The permit covers qualifying runoff that reaches state surface waters, including through a storm drain.

title: Pumping groundwater from some wells requires a permit
brief: The state rule applies to nonexempt wells in designated groundwater management areas. Buying water from a utility is a different case.

title: Data centers must measure noise before and after construction
brief: The city requires a sound study before construction and annual studies at peak operation for five years after construction.

title: Standalone data centers need planned-area zoning
brief: Chandler restricts sites whose main use is a data center to planned area developments. A server facility that supports another business follows different size and location rules.

title: Marana must approve a plan that specifically allows a data center
brief: For a standalone data center, the town must adopt a site-specific plan or amendment through rezoning. The approval may cover only part of the site.

title: Marana Water will not supply drinking water for data center cooling
brief: Developers must identify a different supply for cooling and humidity control. The restriction does not rule out drinking water for other building uses.

title: How many parking spaces does a data center need?
brief: Mesa requires one space per 5,000 square feet for the first 200,000 square feet and one per 10,000 square feet above that.

title: Mesa requires council approval for standalone industrial sites
brief: A standalone data center in a general or heavy industrial district needs specific council approval through the planned area development process.

title: When must an operator apply to the Navajo Nation for an air permit?
New or modified equipment can need an air permit before construction
Santa Fe County paused some large data center approvals

Larger direct withdrawals must be registered
Boone County paused new data center applications
brief: The pause covers land under county zoning outside incorporated towns and cities, from June 16, 2026 through June 15, 2027. It excludes facilities that provide internal computing for a business on the same campus.

title: High-capacity water withdrawals must be registered
brief: Owners must register if their equipment can withdraw more than 100,000 gallons in one day. This is a reporting requirement, not permission to withdraw water.

title: Applicants need the electric utility to confirm available power
brief: The utility must confirm that it can serve the facility and the area without interfering with other customers’ service.

title: An industrial site still needs county zoning approval
brief: In unincorporated Lake County, data centers need a special exception in two industrial districts. Being on industrial land does not by itself allow construction.

title: Cooling water must be delivered to the site
brief: The county requires a closed cooling loop that does not lose water to evaporation. A data center cannot use a local well, town water or surface water for cooling.

title: A small server room can be exempt from data center rules
brief: The county excludes small server rooms that support another permitted use.

title: Data centers must recirculate cooling water
brief: Developers can propose an alternative if they show that it uses less water and less energy than a closed loop.

title: Developers must submit a water supply study
brief: Projects that rely on a nonpublic water source must also submit a study every two years after operations begin.

title: Phoenix reviews power, fire safety and noise before zoning approval
Wabash County paused new data center permits
Two districts allow a data center after township approval
brief: A developer can seek conditional use approval in the Commercial Business or Industrial Business district. The township requires a site of at least 50 acres.

title: A data center must sit 150 feet back from a residential boundary
brief: The setback covers the data center and its accessory uses where the property line directly borders residential use or residential zoning.

title: The township checks noise before and after construction
brief: The developer must study outdoor equipment noise and submit a second study six months after the center reaches full operation.

title: The utility must approve service to the site
brief: The developer must show the public utility approved its application for service. Public water and sewer must meet the proposed use.

title: Boulder County limits data centers to under 50 kW
brief: The county allows centers below 50 kilowatts in its Light Industrial and General Industrial districts. The change covers unincorporated land; cities set their own zoning.

title: State environmental permits depend on local approvals
brief: For qualifying data center permits, Pennsylvania DEP requires proof that the project fits the local comprehensive plan and has received the applicable local zoning and subdivision approvals.

title: Land use approval for work that may harm coastal resources
brief: A developer proposing work that could harm coastal resources must apply for a land use permit unless the law exempts the work.

title: Clearing or construction may need coastal approval
brief: If the project falls under coastal management jurisdiction, the developer must obtain written approval before work starts. Major siting applications require a public hearing.

title: Coastal zoning review in the first tier
brief: The territory reviews proposed development in its designated first-tier coastal zone. Check the parcel boundary before assuming coastal review applies.

title: Where to apply for a building permit in Guam
brief: Guam accepts building permit applications at the Business License and Permit Center at Public Works in Upper Tumon. The center brings together land management, fire and other reviewing agencies.

title: Atlanta restricts data centers near transit stops
brief: Atlanta prohibits new data centers within half a mile of a MARTA rail station or future bus rapid transit stop covered by the zoning amendment.

title: New data centers are prohibited along the Beltline overlay
brief: Atlanta prohibits new data centers in the Beltline Overlay District. Use the mapped district boundary to check a parcel.

title: No drinking water for evaporative chillers
brief: Aurora bars evaporative chillers that use potable water. The restriction applies to data centers seeking conditional use approval.

title: Water use is capped per unit of computing energy
brief: A data center may use at most 0.2 liters of potable building water per kilowatt-hour consumed by its IT equipment.

title: Ground-level chillers must be 1,000 feet from sensitive uses
brief: Measure from the nearest part of the equipment yard to the property line of a home, hospital or educational use. A later neighboring use does not undo an existing conditional approval.

title: Model water use before the city hears the application
brief: A third-party engineer must model water consumption and water quality. The report covers supply sources, average and peak demand, and cooling and water reuse plans.

title: Measure existing noise for a week
brief: The first application must include a week of baseline noise measurements. A separate acoustical study must model compliance with the applicable limits.

title: Outdoor cooling equipment needs noise controls
brief: Santa Clara requires structural noise controls on exterior cooling fans and equipment. The city’s community development director decides whether measures such as baffles or acoustic louvers are sufficient.

title: Point outdoor lighting down and into the site
brief: Santa Clara requires fully shielded exterior lights that direct light away from adjoining roads and properties.

Randolph County uses a special industrial zoning district
brief: A site must be in the Heavy Industrial Conditional District. A general industrial designation does not give the project permission by right.

title: Keep outdoor equipment 1,000 feet from homes and schools
brief: The same minimum distance applies to daycares, churches, hospitals, camps, parks and other listed community facilities.

title: An engineer must certify the cooling plan
brief: The plan must minimize water use. For a liquid-cooled facility, it must also identify the water source and daily use.

title: Grid connection is required before occupancy
brief: Backup generators may run during grid emergencies. Routine testing is limited to four hours per month.

title: Two county permits are required
brief: In the area zoned by Brown County, a data center needs conditional use approval and a building permit. The rule also covers changes beyond routine maintenance.

title: The usual buffer is one mile
brief: The county measures between property lines. A shorter distance requires noise evidence and can never be less than half a mile.

title: Grid-connected projects need the utility’s approval
brief: The operator must show that the utility has the capacity and infrastructure to serve the project. Off-grid systems are exempt.

title: Springdale classifies electronic data storage as an office use
brief: The definition includes computer equipment used to process, store or route electronic data. Check the parcel’s district separately.

title: Large facilities must stay a quarter-mile from homes, schools and churches
brief: Pitt County also requires a 50-foot buffer inside the site boundary and limits height to 35 feet, except for transmission lines and utility poles.

title: A sound study must accompany the site plan
brief: The application must show nearby homes, churches and schools, describe the project, and carry the owner’s and operator’s signatures.

title: Two village districts allow data processing facilities by right
brief: The Commercial and Light Industrial & Warehousing districts allow the village’s defined mainframe facilities. An ordinary office does not qualify under that definition.

title: Parking is capped at four spaces per 1,000 square feet
brief: This is a maximum in both districts where the village allows data processing facilities.

title: Only the C-3 Commercial district allows data centers
brief: The operator must also get a special use permit. The rule covers facilities that store, process or distribute data remotely.

title: Include a sound study and equipment layout
brief: The application must describe the project, access and screening and include an acoustical engineer’s findings and proposed noise controls.

title: Get the utility’s approval before installation
brief: Grid-connected systems need evidence of that approval. Off-grid systems are exempt.

title: Data centers need special approval in four county districts
brief: In unincorporated Douglas County, the code allows a data center to apply in OI, LI, LI-R or HI. It does not allow this use in the other districts in the table.

title: Submit the utility schedule with the site plan
brief: The county asks for a construction schedule, a utility schedule and a master site plan showing any required parcel splits or combinations.

title: A data center cannot share a property line with residential land
brief: The county applies this restriction when the neighboring land is zoned for housing or is already used for housing.

title: Leave a 100-foot buffer near residential land
brief: If the project is within 200 feet of residential land, the county requires an undisturbed buffer. The director may reduce the buffer after reviewing the design and screening. The ban on sharing a property line still applies.
